prior_importants.description: The new advice for answered threads, "open a new round", sends the operator to `pup fix`, which refuses again with the same advice while the answered threads stay unresolved and nobody has commented on them since; the one step that makes a round possible, a reply on the thread, was dropped from both messages.

findings.description: The advice to reply as the operator and re-run pup fix loops when the re-run round makes no commit: its gated sha equals the previous round's, the sha-only marker check suppresses its reply and summary, the thread stays unanswered, and ci wait keeps naming pup fix.
findings.body:
**Problem:** the new advice (reply on the thread as the operator, then re-run `pup fix`) loops if the re-run round commits nothing. That is the likely outcome, since the advice itself says the worker sees only the bot's finding.

**How it happens:**
1. Round 1 declines thread T and gates at sha `S1`. Its reply on T carries `<!-- pup fix-round S1 -->`, so T reads `isAnswered`.
2. The operator replies on T and re-runs `pup fix`. T now reads unanswered, so `reviewVerdict` relays it. The worker declines again and commits nothing.
3. The gate has no refusal for a round with no commit. The only worktree check is the dirty-tree one (`merge-gate.service.ts:1884`). Fresh-base passes with "already based on" (`merge-gate.service.ts:1923-1930`), and `sha = resolveCommit(branchRef)` (L1982) gives `S1` again. The push is a no-op, `recordMerge` records `S1`, and `answerFixRoundThreads` runs.
4. `fixRoundMarker(sha)` builds the same string as round 1. `thread.ownReplies.some((body) => body.includes(marker))` (`fix-round.service.ts:346`) matches round 1's reply, so the decline is not posted on T. The PR summary, including its `@claude review` ask, is skipped the same way (L361).

This assumes the local target branch did not move between the two rounds. If it did, the auto-merge makes a new sha and the replies post normally.

**Result:** the operator's comment stays the newest counted comment on T, so `isAnswered` stays false (`github.client.ts:476-479`). `pup ci wait` names `pup fix <id>` again (`ci-wait.service.ts:297-299`), and `pup fix` relays T again. Each repeat climbs the model ladder until the top-rung refusal, and an override lets it keep going. The round's decline never reaches GitHub; the only trace is a console line from the gate.

**Root cause:** the dedup marker is keyed only on the gated sha. It cannot tell a re-gate of the same round apart from a new round that ends on the same sha. This was harmless while answered threads were never relayed again, but this PR's advice now leads to exactly that case.

**Fix options:**
- Key the marker on the round too, for example the `fix_round` event's id. A re-gate of the same round still finds its own posts, and a new round posts again.
- Or skip a thread only when its newest marked own reply is also its newest counted comment.

process_issues.description: Round 5 budget: conventions, docs, context, simplicity and maintainability were not spawned. Spec had no source (no closing issues), and workflow-safety had nothing to check (no workflow change). Security ran as a single instance despite the size gate: its trust-boundary surface is narrow (three files). The consolidator was not spawned because only one finding came back, so there was nothing to merge.
